references.text: God's angel calls to Hagar from heaven when she is in the wilderness with Ishmael, a direct parallel to the Lord's angel who finds Hagar at the water spring in the wilderness.
The Lord's angel calls to Abraham from heaven, another important case where the Lord's angel (מלאך יהוה) intervenes in a crisis situation.
Hagar gives a name to the One who spoke to her, and the well is called Beer-Lahai-Roi – a direct follow-up to the meeting at the water spring in v.7.
Ishmael's descendants settled from Havilah to Shur, a geographical link to 'the way to Shur' where Hagar was found.
The Lord's angel appears to Moses in a burning thorn bush – an important example of the Lord's angel revealing himself to people.
Israel sets out into the Wilderness of Shur after crossing the Red Sea, the same geographical area mentioned in Gen 16:7.
The Lord's angel appears to Gideon and speaks to him, another important example of the Lord's angel seeking out people in difficult situations.
Deuteronomy illuminates the theological background for God's active search and care for the lonely in the wilderness.
